findings.statement: Independently re-derived (not trusted): all 7 SSOT guards in check_ssot_consistency.py genuinely die when surgically, individually reverted in a scratch tree. Each revert (word-order binding/F-COMMA-ADJACENCY, F-REGEX-SILENT-ZERO, F-SYMLINK-ESCAPE, F-DESC-MEASURE-DECOUPLE, F-FROZEN-ROLE-SMUGGLE, F-CONTROLLING-DATE-GAP, and the affirmative-coverage/F-NEGATION-CLOSED-VOCAB inversion) kills EXACTLY one test in test_ssot_consistency.py (85 passed/1 failed each time, no collateral), and in every case the failing assertion targets the guard's own specific on-topic diagnostic string or the checker's overall ok/exit status -- not an unrelated baseline. This confirms the coordinator's '7 of 7 SSOT guards die when reverted' claim under independent adversarial re-derivation, and finds no third undiscriminating fixture beyond the two the coordinator's own record already admits.
assumptions_used: A 'guard' is counted at the granularity of the 7 named round-9 defect classes (F-COMMA-ADJACENCY, F-REGEX-SILENT-ZERO, F-SYMLINK-ESCAPE, F-DESC-MEASURE-DECOUPLE, F-FROZEN-ROLE-SMUGGLE, F-CONTROLLING-DATE-GAP, F-NEGATION-CLOSED-VOCAB), matching the 7 attack fixtures under the 'Round 9' section of test_ssot_consistency.py plus their 3 control fixtures.

Mutations were surgical (neutralised exactly one guard's condition/branch) rather than reverting to the whole pre-915e2e4 file, to avoid conflating guards that share code (e.g. word-order binding and affirmative-coverage both touch find_assertions).

Every mutation kills exactly its targeted fixture(s) with no collateral, and every failure is on the guard's own specific message. Confirms 'canary guards die when reverted' under independent adversarial re-derivation, whichever of the two defensible countings ('5' or '7') is used.
assumptions_used: '5 of 5 guards' is read as the conceptual grouping (staleness / supersession / id-resolution / digest-field-validation / non-file-exclusion) rather than a literal 1:1 mapping to the 7 independently mutable code branches, since this grouping is the only one that reconciles with the stated '10 canary regression cases' test count.

findings.statement: Swept every consumer of find_assertions() (which changed its return shape from 3-tuples to 4-tuples in 915e2e4) across the whole repository. Exactly two call sites exist, both inside check_ssot_consistency.py: check_status_assertions (unpacks 'number, identifier, status, affirmative') and _matching_exemption (unpacks '_line, _id, found_status, _aff'). Both correctly unpack the new 4-tuple. find_board_assertions still legitimately returns 3-tuples and find_assertions correctly widens them ('(n, i, s, True) for n, i, s in board'). No test file calls either function directly (all test coverage is black-box subprocess). The unpacking-mismatch class that 'already bit once during the fix pass and was found only by a crashing test' does not recur anywhere in the current tree.

findings.statement: Audited the measurement machinery (F-SSOT-10) for a fail-open path, focusing on the one place the module docstring says was 'deliberately made non-strict' (_measured_path's use of Path.resolve(strict=False), to preserve a more specific 'unreadable' diagnosis for a merely-missing file rather than a vaguer containment error). Traced every return-None branch in _measured_path/measure_fact/_count_lines_matching/_json_array_length/_read_measured_file: each is paired with an errors.append() in the same branch, with no bare skip. Confirmed live: a genuinely missing measurement target still produces the specific 'cannot be run...unreadable...never a skip' error (test_f_ssot_10_unreadable_measurement_target_is_an_error_not_a_skip passes), and an in-tree symlink escaping the repository is still followed and caught (test_f_r9_in_tree_symlink_pointing_outside_the_repo_is_refused passes, and reverting only that check makes it fail cleanly with no other change in behaviour -- see F-001 guard G3). No path was found where a failed/unrunnable measurement leaves the checker's errors list empty; check_facts()'s errors list is checked unconditionally by main(), so any single populated error anywhere forces exit 1 regardless of which check populated it.
assumptions_used: 'The measurement changes altered several error messages and one of them was deliberately made non-strict' in the assignment refers to the resolve()/containment logic in _measured_path, the only spot in the file carrying an explicit 'NON-strict' comment.
reproduction: grep -n "NON-strict" .agent-harness/scripts/check_ssot_consistency.py to locate the one deliberately-non-strict spot

findings.statement: The narrowing of the frozen-role live-region guard from 'all non-current roles' to 'role==frozen' alone does NOT reopen the specific hole it was built to close (test_f_r9_frozen_role_cannot_sit_in_a_live_region still passes at HEAD; git-diffed the historical-role handling branch and it is byte-identical between 5c198c0, pre-915e2e4, and HEAD, so nothing was reopened there). However, the record's stated justification for exempting role=historical -- 'already constrained by the same-line commit test... licence earned by content rather than position' -- is empirically false. Using ONLY the stock test fixture's own already-declared data (no fabricated fact, no fabricated prior value), adding one extra role=historical assertion site and planting 'There are 35 hook tests actually (ed7bc49)' in the always-live SHARED_CONTEXT.md 'Current milestone' bullet (true current value is 39; 35/ed7bc49 is a real, legitimately-declared prior pair from the stock fixture) makes the real, unmutated checker return exit 0 / ok:true. A stale, superseded number reads as a plain present-tense claim in the exact region the F-COMMA-ADJACENCY and F-D065-05 attacks target, with the only 'protection' being a bare, unconstrained substring match for a commit-looking token. This is a live, unremediated instance of the F-D065-05 defect class (a stated fact diverging from reality with no machine check) via an adjacent, un-audited path; it predates 915e2e4 rather than being introduced by it, but 915e2e4's own comment and the D-070-B9/B10 frozen row both assert a protection that does not hold under adversarial testing.
assumptions_used: The threat model treated is the same one the module's own docstring already assumes for role=frozen and for SSOT_FACTS.json generally: an editor who can write both SSOT_FACTS.json and the live prose surface. This is not a new or unfair assumption -- it is the exact threat model the frozen-role fix, and the whole F-D065-05 lineage, is built against.

findings.statement: The test_hooks.py `_repinned_validator` fixture change (copying check_ssot_consistency.py and check_canary_freshness.py alongside _harness.py into the fixture's temp scripts dir) is a genuine, correctly-scoped bug fix and does not weaken any existing fixture. Reverting it in isolation (copying only _harness.py, as before 32ba566) against the current validate_harness.py reproduces exactly the claimed regression: both test_legacy_manifest_pin_survives_a_commit and test_legacy_manifest_pin_cannot_be_dropped_by_deleting_its_declaration fail with payload {'errors': ['Canary freshness checker is missing: check_canary_freshness.py'], 'ok': False}. With the fix applied, direct inspection of the full validate_harness.py payload against this fixture shows 'ssot_consistency': 'not applicable (no gate registry)' (correctly scoped out -- this narrow fixture creates no GATE_REGISTRY.json and isn't testing SSOT consistency) and 'canary_freshness': 'ok' (genuinely zero CANARY_ATTESTATION artifacts exist in this fixture, so there is nothing that can be stale -- a legitimate, non-vacuous 'ok', not a bypass). Neither test passes for a new-and-wrong reason.

findings.statement: The claim 'production suites 36 unchanged' (identical wording in both the VALIDATION_LEDGER.md D-070 Part B10 row and the merged FROZEN_DECISIONS.md D-070-B9/B10 row) is unverifiable against the tracked record. `git log --all -S "production suites" -- docs/harness/VALIDATION_LEDGER.md .agent-harness/context/FROZEN_DECISIONS.md` shows this exact phrase first appears in 32ba566 itself, so there is no prior recorded baseline anywhere in the SSOT record for 'unchanged' to be measured against. It is not one of the four facts declared in SSOT_FACTS.json (legacy_results_manifest_entry_count, hook_fixture_count, ssot_regression_case_count, canary_regression_case_count) -- i.e. it is asserted but not mechanically measured by the very tooling this commit chain built specifically to eliminate asserted-but-unmeasured numbers (the F-R9-007 defect class the same commit chain repeatedly criticises). Checked three plausible candidate populations and none is 36: `find tests -maxdepth 1 -name 'test_*.py' | wc -l` = 256 files; `pytest -m production --collect-only -q` = 446 collected test items; `pytest -m gold --collect-only -q` = 105 collected test items. No candidate matching 36 was identified within reasonable effort. This does not prove the claim is false, only that it cannot currently be checked against the record or the repository, which is itself the defect class this project's own SSOT machinery exists to prevent.
assumptions_used: 'Production suites' was interpreted as some countable population of Python test files or pytest-collected items under the top-level tests/ tree (the only 'production' pytest surface with markers named 'production'/'gold'/'release_smoke' etc. in pyproject.toml); no Rust/cargo suite count of 36 was checked, since the two commits under review touch zero Rust lines and the claim appears specifically alongside the Python-harness-suite numbers.
